mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-9.6, -11.9, -17.6, -18.1). This negative momentum reflects an entrenched behavioral pattern of reduced discretionary outings that will persist absent a countervailing shock, continuing to push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite three or more consecutive weeks of prior decline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from 5.6 to -30.1 over four weeks, a magnitude consistent with a new outdoor-gathering restriction. Such restrictions typically extend to retail capacity limits within two weeks, so RETAIL_REC should fall further once the PARKS decline exceeds a severe threshold.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 20 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped 30.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next two weeks despite PARKS having fallen more than 20 points in the prior two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility is recovering sharply (-27.7 to -10.4) while TRANSIT remains roughly flat around -25. The combination of rising workplace attendance without a matching transit rebound suggests commuters are using private transport, which supports incidental retail stops near workplaces, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 17.3 points while TRANSIT changed only 0.0 points t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues declining over the next two weeks even as WORKPLACES rises and TRANSIT stays flat.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility, elevated through the snapshot but ticking down from 16.3 to 12.0, indicates households are beginning to spend less time at home. In an easing-restriction regime this early decline in RESIDENTIAL precedes a rebound in out-of-home retail activity within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 16.3 to 12.0 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL has declined for two consecutive weeks in an easing regime.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point of mid-January precedes Chinese New Year (mid-February) in Singapore, a period historically marked by a surge in retail shopping for festive goods and gifts regardless of current mobility trend, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-01-15 falls within four weeks of Chinese New Year 2021 (Feb 12)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite the approaching Chinese New Year holiday period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has steadily declined from 11.9 to 1.7, indicating the end of a stockpiling or precautionary-purchasing phase. Once GROCERY_PHARM falls below a low single-digit threshold, it signals households have normalized essential shopping, which coincides with reduced urgency-driven retail trips and further RETAIL_REC decline over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM having fallen below 5 percent change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of falling PARKS and falling RETAIL_REC alongside stable TRANSIT indicates a localized substitution effect: as outdoor recreation becomes restricted, people are not redirecting that time into indoor retail trips, because transit demand (a proxy for broader mobility willingness) has not increased. This interaction predicts continued short-term suppression of RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 35.7 points while TRANSIT remained near -25 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next week while PARKS continues to fall and TRANSIT remains flat.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous sharp declines in PARKS and RETAIL_REC over the last two weeks, occurring while WORKPLACES partially recovers, is consistent with a policy regime that permits essential work movement but tightens discretionary and recreational gathering limits. Under this tightening-restriction regime, RETAIL_REC should remain suppressed or fall further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and RETAIL_REC both decline for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES rises
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and RETAIL_REC fell together in t-1w and t-0w while WORKPLACES rose
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite continued joint decline in PARKS and RETAIL_REC alongside rising WORKPLACES.
